source_name: CaSys — Интернационален Картичен Систем АД Скопје (career/company site)
why_relevant: The country's only Visa/Mastercard-certified independent processor and personalisation bureau. Its hiring (IT support, customer service, processing roles) is the single richest indirect window on the switch/authorisation, ATM and POS management platform used by most MK issuers — i.e. the incumbent to displace or partner with.

source_name: Bintern — MK applicant-tracking/careers host used by local employers
why_relevant: Hosts the canonical, full-text career pages for MK employers including CaSys; ad bodies here are longer and less edited than aggregator republications, so technology requirements survive intact.

source_name: Pazar3.mk — Работа / ИТ сектор classifieds
why_relevant: Highest-volume MK classifieds site; smaller vendors, integrators, POS/ATM service firms and outsourced bank support roles advertise here rather than on premium boards — catches the long tail of payments-adjacent hiring that vrabotuvanje misses.

source_name: Vraboti.se — MK job portal, IT/Informatics categories
why_relevant: Second-tier MK board with category filters for Информатичка технологија / Информатика; surfaced directly on card-system keyword searching, so its ad bodies are indexed and searchable for platform names.

source_name: Kariera.mk — employment portal with CV profiles
why_relevant: Job portal where candidates upload CVs and apply in one click; the employer-side listings carry stack requirements and the platform positions itself as a central MK employment hub. CV side is candidate-owned personal data — treat listings only.

source_name: JobMatch.mk — automated tracker/statistics of MK IT job ads
why_relevant: Purpose-built tool that automatically tracks MK IT job ads and extracts statistics — most-demanded skills, most-posted positions, posting volume over time. That is exactly the A6 weak-signal aggregation layer: it can reveal rising demand for a named banking/payments technology before any vendor announcement.

source_name: IT.mk — ИТ Кариера section and forum
why_relevant: MK IT community media running a careers feed plus a forum thread on job-ad platforms; doubles as a pointer to new hiring channels (it surfaced JobMatch) and as commentary on which employers/stacks are hiring.

source_name: LinkedIn Jobs — Skopje / North Macedonia
why_relevant: Where MK banks, ASEE/Asseco, Printec-type vendors and outsourcers post English-language engineering roles that name products explicitly (Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, ISO 8583, Java/Oracle stacks). Volume in-country is meaningful (hundreds of open Skopje roles, ~240 engineering).

source_name: LinkedIn member profiles / CVs of MK banking-IT staff
why_relevant: Individual CVs state the platforms people ran inside named MK banks — e.g. a Skopje developer profile describing support for a migration to Oracle FLEXCUBE. This is the strongest per-bank vendor-attribution signal in the whole cell, though it is personal data.

source_name: Toptal / freelancer marketplace resumes for Skopje developers
why_relevant: Publicly published CVs outside LinkedIn's login wall; the one found names Oracle FLEXCUBE migration work and cross-check reporting in a Macedonian banking context — proof that marketplace resumes leak incumbent core-banking products.

source_name: Joberty — MK IT employer profiles, reviews and tech-stack listings
why_relevant: Regional employer-review site with company pages for MK payments/banking IT actors (CaSys/Интернационален Картичен Систем, Asseco North Macedonia) that expose declared technology stacks, salaries and open roles — employee-sourced confirmation of vendor products in use.

source_name: ASEE / Asseco SEE — career centre and Skopje entity hiring
why_relevant: Asseco SEE DOOEL Skopje (ex-Pexim Macedonia, renamed 2009, HQ 17 Naroden Front St.) is the dominant regional banking-software vendor and a direct competitor/partner. Its Skopje job ads reveal which of its banking products (e-banking, e-commerce, payments, system integration) it staffs locally, and therefore which MK bank projects it is running.

source_name: Printec Group — Workable job-openings portal (CEE incl. MK)
why_relevant: Printec's own ATS lists openings across its 16 CEE countries; MK-located roles and their required skills indicate which local bank projects and transaction-technology lines are staffing up. Also the reference template for reading rival vendors' ATS feeds.

source_name: Nextsense DOO Skopje — hiring footprint (finance/telecom digital solutions)
why_relevant: MK ICT vendor (~88 staff) building digital solutions for government and Finance; its engineering vacancies indicate the integration, identity/e-signature and digital-channel stacks it deploys into MK banks. Glassdoor showed no openings at time of search — hiring is episodic, so it is a low-frequency signal.

source_name: Glassdoor — Skopje employer salary and openings pages
why_relevant: Employee-reported job titles and salaries per MK employer; title taxonomies ('Card Systems Administrator', 'Core Banking Developer') corroborate which platform teams exist inside a bank or vendor even when no ad is currently live.

source_name: MojaPlata.mk — MK salary survey by position and sector
why_relevant: Largest MK online salary survey (~20,000 respondents), with averages by position, sector and region and paid professional salary reports. Position taxonomies for banking/IT roles and pay movement are a soft indicator of where banks are building internal platform teams versus outsourcing to vendors.

source_name: FINKI (Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering, UKIM) — job-ad board
why_relevant: Banks recruit graduates through the faculty and post full ads there — e.g. an NBRSM (central bank) programmer vacancy in the Applications Directorate specifying MS Visual Studio and MS SQL Server, a direct read on the regulator's in-house development stack. Faculty boards often carry ads never posted commercially.

source_name: CareerHub / MladiHub — MK youth careers platform company pages
why_relevant: Hosts employer pages for payments actors including Интернационален картичен систем (КаСис); internship and junior ads here describe the day-to-day systems more plainly than senior ads, which often makes the product name explicit.

source_name: MASIT — ICT Chamber of Commerce member directory
why_relevant: Not a job board, but the authoritative roster of MK ICT companies (CaSys is a listed member) from which to build the employer watchlist that all the hiring monitors are then keyed on — the actor map that makes cell #11 systematic rather than opportunistic.

source_name: KIBS AD Skopje (Клириншка куќа КИБС) — corporate site / news
why_relevant: Operator of the MK interbank net-settlement system for small payments and of KIBSTrust (PKI/e-signature). Its hiring would name the clearing, instant-payments and PKI platforms at the centre of the national payment infrastructure — the highest-value single technical disclosure in the market. No vacancy page was located in this pass.

source_name: MKJOB — AI job-search platform for North Macedonia (launch covered by Bankarstvo)
why_relevant: Newly launched MK AI job-matching platform; new aggregators re-index ads that expire elsewhere and may expose structured skill fields, so it is worth evaluating as an additional harvesting surface. Canonical product URL not yet confirmed.

source_name: NBRSM — Conference on Payments and Market Infrastructures ("Let's Get Digital") / Платни системи section
source_subtype: central bank conference agenda / participant list
why_relevant: The National Bank's recurring payments & market infrastructure conference publishes participant lists (named individuals + institutions incl. Halkbank, Stopanska banka) and agendas. Participant rosters are the single richest MK-specific map of who owns payments/digital budgets inside each bank, plus which vendors attend.

source_name: Македонска банкарска асоцијација (MBA) — Активности / news
why_relevant: The banking association reports on the conferences its member banks attend and organise (trainings, payment-services events, regional summits), and tags posts by bank. A pointer-rich chronology of MK bank participation with dates.

source_name: МАСИТ (MASIT) — Chamber of ICT, events & annual conference (MASIT 2.0 "Recode Reality")
source_subtype: ICT chamber event pages / member & partner lists
why_relevant: MASIT runs the flagship MK ICT annual conference plus specialised finance events (e.g. a dedicated SEPA transfers event). Its patron/partner scheme exposes bank-vendor alignment — Halkbank AD appears as MASIT Patron Partner and hosted a 2025 event on its premises.

source_name: MASIT — специјализиран настан: СЕПА трансфери, национални капацитети и патот кон интеграција
why_relevant: A single-topic MK event on SEPA integration — exactly the procurement wave payments vendors chase. Speaker list identifies bank and regulator people driving SEPA readiness.

source_name: Асоцијација за е-трговија на Македонија (AETM / ecommerce.mk) — Регионална конференција за е-трговија
why_relevant: The flagship MK e-commerce/payments conference (8th edition at the National Opera and Ballet, Skopje). Publishes agendas and named sponsor tiers; reported sponsors include Kasys and Payton as gold, Mastercard as general partner, A1 Macedonia as digital partner, plus Komercijalna banka as sponsor — a direct card/acquiring vendor-to-bank signal.

source_name: Ecommerce Awards Macedonia (ecommerceawards.mk)
why_relevant: National e-commerce awards with ~38 awards across 18 categories including a payment-experience category. Nominee and winner lists name merchants, PSPs and the banks/processors behind their checkout — an annual ranked map of who is winning MK online payments.
